summary.text: A 45-year-old woman and smoker presented in March 2020 with dyspnea and chest pain. Work-up showed a primary pulmonary adenocarcinoma, ALK-rearrangement positive with PD-L1 above 50%, involving the pleura, liver and bones, staged IV cT3N3M1c. First-line alectinib 600 mg twice daily was started in April 2020 with an excellent clinical and radiological response.

In July 2020 liver enzymes and bilirubin rose, with fatigue and anorexia; hepatitis B, C and HIV tests were negative and liver ultrasonography showed fewer liver metastases and mild steatosis. Hemoglobin then fell from 121 to 112 g/L with elevated LDH and reticulocytes, low haptoglobin, negative Coombs tests and acanthocytes, echinocytes and spherocytes on smear. ANA was non-specifically positive, and the erythrocyte enzymatic panel was normal.

She was diagnosed with grade 3 liver toxicity and alectinib-induced Coombs-negative hemolytic anemia. Alectinib was stopped as of late August 2020 and aminotransferases, bilirubin, LDH and hemoglobin gradually normalized. After a 4-week recovery period, second-line brigatinib was started in October 2020 and no further similar laboratory perturbations were noted.

Table 2 lists hemoglobin 112 g/L, MCV 92 fL, platelets 306, LDH 575 U/L, indirect and total bilirubin 31 and 65 μmol/L, haptoglobin below 0.3 g/L, reticulocytes 105.8 and a negative Coombs test upon diagnosis of hemolytic anemia on alectinib.

summary.text: An 80-year-old woman and smoker with severe aortic stenosis and baseline normocytic anemia of chronic disease (Hb 106 g/L) was found, during aortic valve replacement work-up, to have a large left lung lesion, mediastinal nodes and a single brain metastasis. Endoscopic biopsy showed ALK-positive lung adenocarcinoma, PD-L1 above 50%, stage IV cT4N3M1b, and alectinib 600 mg BID was started in October 2019.

In early November 2019 she showed a significant radiologic response but was hospitalized for rapid atrial fibrillation with cardiac insufficiency and worsening anemia, with Hb 67 g/L, raised LDH and reticulocytes, low haptoglobin, negative Coombs and G6PD tests and acanthocytes and echinocytes on smear. She received transfusions, IV iron, erythropoietin and cardiac optimization, and endoscopies were negative for blood loss.

With persistent hemolysis and Hb of 80-90 g/L, alectinib was reduced to 450 mg BID in March 2020 and stopped in early April 2020, with Hb rising to 133 g/L. After TAVI in early June 2020, alectinib was rechallenged in late June, the hemolytic picture recurred and it was permanently discontinued in July 2020. Brigatinib was started in August 2020 and laboratory tests improved rapidly, confirming alectinib-related hemolytic anemia; serial values are in Table 1.

Table 2 lists, upon diagnosis of hemolytic anemia on alectinib, hemoglobin 67 g/L, LDH 361 U/L, indirect and total bilirubin 25 and 52 μmol/L, haptoglobin below 0.3 g/L and a negative Coombs test; the Table 1 serial panel for this patient is recorded separately.

summary.text: A 48-year-old non-smoking woman with no previous medical condition and a strong family history of malignancy presented in late October 2019 with dry cough, difficulty breathing, dizziness and occasional loss of equilibrium. Work-up showed metastatic left lower lobe lung adenocarcinoma with 3 brain lesions, cT2N2M1c, ALK rearrangement positive and PD-L1 70%. Alectinib 600 mg BID started on 1 November 2019 gave a remarkable clinical and radiologic response.

In late February 2020 indirect bilirubin rose to 26.6 μmol/L with elevated LDH, increased reticulocytes and low haptoglobin, Hb 114 g/L, normal other liver enzymes, vitamin B12 and folate, negative Coombs tests and acanthocytes, echinocytes, spherocytes and anisocytosis on smear. An alectinib-related hemolytic process was suspected and alectinib was held for 2 weeks, with some laboratory improvement.

Alectinib was resumed for 3 weeks and the hemolytic process recurred more pronouncedly, with scleral icterus, dark urine and fatigue, Hb 119 g/L, bilirubin 37 μmol/L, LDH 243, haptoglobin below 0.3 g/L and the same smear findings. Alectinib was finally stopped and changed to brigatinib in June 2020, with resolution of hemolysis and jaundice and return of all laboratory tests to the normal range.

Table 2 lists, upon diagnosis of hemolytic anemia on alectinib, hemoglobin 114 g/L, LDH 285 U/L, indirect and total bilirubin 26 and 39 μmol/L, haptoglobin 0.08 g/L, reticulocytes 110 and a negative Coombs test.

summary.text: A 69-year-old never-smoking woman of Chinese origin presented with progressively worsening dyspnea and was diagnosed with stage IV ALK-positive, PD-L1-negative lung adenocarcinoma with all other mutations negative. Alectinib 600 mg twice daily was started in February 2022.

In early March 2022 Hb dropped from 126 to 101 g/L with MCV 80 fL, normal iron, B12, folate and TSH, indirect hyperbilirubinemia reaching 21 μmol/L, elevated LDH and reticulocytes, decreased haptoglobin and a negative Coombs test. The peripheral smear proved hemolysis, and with no other new medication she was considered to have alectinib-induced hemolytic anemia.

Because hemolysis was asymptomatic with Hb stable around 100 g/L and a good response to treatment, alectinib dosing was not changed. She remains on the same dose with persistent mild chronic hemolysis and no symptoms, under close observation.

Table 2 lists, upon diagnosis of hemolytic anemia on alectinib, hemoglobin 101 g/L, MCV 80 fL, platelets 414, LDH 298 U/L, indirect and total bilirubin 21 and 27 μmol/L, haptoglobin below 0.3 g/L, reticulocytes 230 and a negative Coombs test.
